sections.content: You know passive *se* and impersonal *se* from B2 Unit 19: with a thing the verb agrees (*Se venden casas*), with a particular person introduced by *a* the verb stays singular (*Se busca a los responsables*). Offices live on this contrast. A notice says what happens to documents and what happens to people, and leaves out who does it: *Se tramitarán las solicitudes*, *Se atenderá a los usuarios por orden de llegada*. For a polite request it uses *se ruega*: *Se ruega a los usuarios hacer cola*. The agreement rule is the one place where a careful notice shows its quality.

sections.title: Things agree, people with a do not
rows: Se tramitarán las solicitudes en la oficina.
Applications will be processed in the office. (a thing: plural verb)
Se sellan los documentos en la ventanilla.
Documents are stamped at the counter. (a thing: plural verb)
Se atenderá a los usuarios por orden de llegada.
Users will be attended to in order of arrival. (people with a: singular)
Se ruega a los usuarios hacer cola.
Users are kindly asked to queue. (a request: singular)

sections.content: The common mistake is a plural verb with *a* + people: *Se atenderán a los usuarios* is wrong, because the people are the object, so nothing can agree with them. Without the *a* the sentence is wrong in the other direction: *Se atenderá los usuarios*. Ask whether you are talking about things (plural verb) or about particular people (*a* and a singular verb).
